description: The bar chart, titled "Can 1B LLM Surpass 405B LLM Rethinking Compute-Optimal Test-Time Scaling," presents a comparative analysis of various large language models (LLMs) across two benchmark datasets, MATH-500 and AIME24, under different scaling strategies. The chart is divided into six subplots (a-f), each illustrating the performance of different models or model configurations. In subplot (a), which compares models on MATH-500, the 3B model (Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct) achieves a score of 78.2, outperforming the 405B model (CoT) with 71.4. Subplot (b) shows that the 1.5B model (DeepSeek-R1-Distill-1.5B) scores 91.6, surpassing the unquantized 1.5B model (GPT-4o) at 90.0 and the unquantized 405B model (TTS) at 85.5. Subplot (c) compares models on MATH-500, where the 671B model (Llama-3.1-405B-Instruct) scores 97.3, the 7B model (DeepSeek-R1) scores 95.2, and the unquantized 7B model (ol1) scores 94.8. Subplot (d), also on MATH-500, shows that the 3B model (Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct) scores 30.0, the 405B model (Llama-3.1-405B-Instruct) scores 23.3, and the unquantized 405B model (ol1) scores 9.3. Subplot (e), on AIME24, shows that the unquantized 1.5B model (GPT-4o) scores 63.6, the 1.5B model (DeepSeek-R1-Distill-1.5B) scores 63.3, and the unquantized 1.5B model (ol1) scores 44.6. Finally, subplot (f) on AIME24 shows that the 7B model (DeepSeek-R1) scores 83.3, the 671B model (DeepSeek-R1) scores 79.8, and the unquantized 671B model (ol1) scores 79.2. The chart uses different colors and patterns to represent different models and their configurations, with the y-axis representing the score and the x-axis representing the model or configuration. The results suggest that smaller models can sometimes outperform larger models, particularly when using test-time scaling strategies.
